title: Wire the durable delivery outbox into the real Telegram transport (dedupe is in-memory only)
description:
Two in-memory structures sit on the live delivery path:

1. `src/transports/telegram.ts:485` — `private outboxByChat = new Map<string, Promise<unknown>>()`: a per-chat promise chain that serialises sends. It is process-local, so anything accepted-but-not-yet-sent at a crash evaporates.
2. `src/transports/telegram.ts:39-63` — `TelegramDuplicateGuard` with `DUPLICATE_WINDOW_MS = 30_000` (telegram.ts:14), a `Map` of `chatId\0payload → sentAt`. Also process-local.

Consequences:
- A crash between "turn produced a message" and "message reached Telegram" loses the message with no record that it was owed. There is no recovery path at boot: the outbox is empty because it never existed.
- Dedupe does not survive a restart: a replay of the same `dedupeKey` (questions use `dedupeKey: question:<qid>`, bot.ts uses others) after reopen is a fresh send. Conversely, the 30s window is also too short to protect a slow retry path within one process.
- `data/state.json` (persisted by `src/core/bot.ts:1113-1126`) contains only `chats, agentChats, minimalChats, goals, pendingSubBots, pendingSubBotIds` — no delivery state at all.

Existing solution that is NOT wired: `src/durable/telegram-surface.ts` — `attachTelegramSurface({transport, satellite, outboxPath})` already implements exactly-once requestIds per chat+message, a JSON outbox with pending/delivered/failed statuses, `SETTLED_RETENTION_MS = 7 days`, and corrupt-outbox quarantine (renamed `.corrupt-<ts>`, deliberately not replayed). Its only caller today is `scripts/durable-satellite.mts`.

Scope to fix:
- Give the live transport a durable send record keyed by `dedupeKey` (or a requestId derived from it) with an explicit unknown/ambiguous state for the crash-mid-send case — do not auto-retry an unknown state, surface it for review.
- Replace or back `TelegramDuplicateGuard` with that durable record so dedupe survives restart.
- Replay owed-but-unsent messages at boot in `bot.start()` order, before new traffic.
- Keep the accepted at-least-once semantics explicit in a comment: a crash right after a successful send may repeat; the guard must make the repeat window durable, not just longer.

Related: pibot-e51 (retry transient send errors), pibot-im7 (poller watchdog), pibot-icv.1 (outbox pattern), pibot-jciq (same class, questions).
acceptance_criteria: After a restart the transport can answer, from durable state, "was this dedupeKey already sent?"; a message accepted before a kill is either sent or recorded as ambiguous at boot — never silently dropped; corrupt outbox state is quarantined and not replayed; tests cover kill-before-send and kill-after-send orderings.
notes:
Implemented and closed. The durable delivery ledger now sits on the live Telegram
push path; nothing is left in memory on that route.

WHAT LANDED

- src/core/delivery-ledger.ts (new) — `DeliveryLedger`, a journal of every outbound
  message the transport accepted responsibility for.
  - States: pending → delivered | failed | unknown.
  - `claim({transport, chatId, dedupeKey, text})` runs BEFORE the first API call and
    returns action `send` | `suppress` (already delivered) | `review` (a previous
    process died mid-send).
  - `beginAttempt(id)` is called before every network attempt, so attempt counts are
    honest and a crash from that instant on is resolvable.
  - At load, a `pending` row with `attempts > 0` becomes `unknown` with
    "process stopped during the send; delivery unconfirmed" — never auto-resent.
  - `DELIVERED_RETENTION_MS` / `FAILED_RETENTION_MS` = 7 days; `MAX_ROWS` = 500
    (oldest settled evicted first, a pending row is NEVER evicted for capacity);
    `MAX_STORED_TEXT` = 4_000 with an ellipsis marker.
  - Row id = sha256(transport + NUL + chatId + NUL + dedupeKey) sliced to 32 hex, so
    the same key in another chat or another transport (sub-bot) is a different row.
  - Atomic 0600 writes; a corrupt row is dropped individually, an unparseable file
    degrades to an empty ledger instead of throwing.
  - In-memory mode when no file is given, so tests and ad-hoc transports are unchanged.
- src/transports/telegram.ts
  - `push()` claims, sends, marks delivered; on error records `failed` for a
    definitive refusal (`isDefinitiveSendRefusal`: 4xx other than 429) and leaves
    anything ambiguous pending, then rethrows exactly as before.
  - `notifyError()` keys its dedupe on `error:<text>` in the same ledger, so repeated
    notices are still suppressed — now across restarts too.
  - `sendPushBody`/`sendClassicMessage`/`sendTelegram` take an `onAttempt` callback,
    invoked before EACH network attempt (including the markup-degrade resend and the
    429/network retries).
  - New `deliveryRecovery()` → { owed, ambiguous } and `replayOwed(row)`.
  - New constructor option `deliveryLedgerPath`; omitted ⇒ in-memory.
  - `TelegramDuplicateGuard` is kept but demoted in its doc comment to the narrow
    cases that need only a short in-process window.
- src/core/bot.ts — `deliveryLedgerPath(agentId?)` → `<dataDir>/deliveries-<agent>.json`
  or `deliveries-main.json` (one file per transport so a sub-bot restart cannot
  rewrite the main bot's owed rows). New `recoverOwedDeliveries()` runs in `start()`
  after `replayOfflineQuestionAnswers()` and before `resolveStarted?.()`: re-sends
  owed rows, logs ambiguous/failed rows to the event log for owner review.
- src/index.ts — main transport passes `deliveryLedgerPath: data/deliveries-main.json`.
- Tests: src/core/delivery-ledger.test.ts (14) and
  src/transports/telegram-delivery.test.ts (11, driving the real push/notifyError
  against a scripted Bot API). Kill-before-send, kill-after-send, restart-suppression,
  cross-chat isolation, definitive refusal, ambiguous non-resend, boot replay,
  0600 mode, in-memory fallback.

GATES: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `npx vitest run` 146 files / 2753 tests pass.

DELIBERATE NON-GOALS / TRADE-OFFS
- Semantics remain at-least-once, now explicit: a crash between a successful send and
  the delivered write yields one duplicate after restart. The alternative (auto-resend
  of unknown rows) trades a visible duplicate for silent loss, which is worse.
- `src/durable/telegram-surface.ts` stays unwired by this fix; it is a satellite
  submission surface (exactly-once model calls), a different concern from outbound
  delivery. Tracked separately by pibot-8ptd.
- Question inline keyboards are not edited after an answer; that remains pibot-jciq's
  documented non-goal and is unaffected here.
close_reason: Durable delivery ledger on the live push path; restart-safe dedupe, owed replay, unknown-never-resent

title: Pending owner questions are not durable — a restart loses them and ask() hangs until timeout
description:
src/core/questions.ts:56-63 keeps `pending` and `pollMap` as plain in-process `Map`s. Nothing about a pending question is written to storage.

Failure: the daemon restarts (deploy, launchd kill, EPIPE, disk-guard recovery) while an agent is blocked in `QuestionBus.ask()`. On reopen the question no longer exists in `pending`, but:

- the owner has already received the message in Telegram (with `dedupeKey: question:<qid>`),
- tapping the button hits a `qid` the process no longer knows → no answer is recorded,
- the agent-side promise is gone entirely, so a resumed session either hangs until `timeoutMs` (default 600e3, capped at 23h) or returns `{timedOut:true}` even though the owner answered.

The restart therefore silently converts an answerable question into a timeout, and the owner gets a stale tap target.

Contrast: the same problem class was solved for the satellite in `src/durable/telegram-surface.ts` (exactly-once requestId per chat+message, pending/delivered/failed outbox, 7-day retention, corrupt-file quarantine) but that module has no production caller.

Scope to fix:
- Persist `QuestionSnapshot` + lifecycle transitions (pending → accepted → answered/cancelled/expired) in a durable store, so `questionSnapshot(qid)`/`pendingSnapshots()` survive a reopen (the dashboard source feed at `subscribeLifecycle` reads them).
- Record the answer durably BEFORE resolving the asking turn; a resumed `ask()` for the same qid must return the recorded answer instead of re-asking.
- Answered-while-offline taps must be replayed at boot (like `CoordinatorRuntime.start()` replays `store.pendingUpdates` before any outbound attempt).
- Expiry must stay authoritative: a question past `pendingUntil` never resolves late.

Related: pibot-ii2 (origin-chat routing), pibot-icv.1 (the satellite outbox pattern to reuse).
acceptance_criteria: Kill the daemon while a question is pending, answer the button while it is down, restart: the resumed ask() returns that answer (not a timeout); a pending question still visible in pendingSnapshots() after reopen; an expired question never resolves late; tests cover kill-then-answer and answer-then-kill orderings.

title: Auto-compaction for agent sessions (percent threshold, ctx.compact, bounded resume)
description:
## Problem
Agent sessions grow past every model's real limit before pi's native auto-compaction fires.

Evidence (2026-10-05): mentalhealthtech's session reached ~512k tokens.
- Pi triggers at `contextTokens > contextWindow - reserveTokens`.
- pibot declares `ollama/glm-5.3-flash:cloud` contextWindow = 1048576, so the trigger sits at ~1.03M.
- The cascade then switched to `openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` (real limit 163840) and every call failed:
  `400 ... requested about 548921 tokens (512069 of text input)`.
- The same runaway run produced the false "finished that turn without a reply" warnings.

pibot builds sessions with `SettingsManager.inMemory({})` and its own `DefaultResourceLoader`,
so `pi install` into `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` never reaches pibot agents.

## Decisions (owner, 2026-10-05)
1. Implement as a pibot plugin modelled on npm:pi-auto-compact (percent threshold + `ctx.compact()`).
2. Trigger = percent of the **active model's declared** context window (upstream parity), configurable.
3. Auto-resume: **yes** - one bounded follow-up after a compaction that interrupted an unfinished turn.

## Design
`src/plugins/auto-compact-plugin.ts` -> `autoCompactPlugin(deps): InlineExtension`, wired in
`agent-manager.ts` next to the capability extensions (host-level, so every agent is protected
without editing private per-agent manifests).

- `input` (only when `event.streamingBehavior === undefined`, i.e. the agent is idle):
  project `usage.tokens + estimateTokens(new message)`; at/over threshold -> `ctx.compact()` and
  await completion before letting the prompt through. No abort, no resume needed.
- `turn_end` (agent mid-run): at/over threshold -> `ctx.compact()` (aborts the run) then queue
  exactly one `[compaction-resume]` follow-up so the interrupted work continues.
  Re-arms only after usage falls back under the threshold.
- Never fail-closed: a hard compaction failure is logged and the prompt proceeds, because
  dropping the owner's message silently is the exact failure mode this work is fixing.
- Config: `<dataDir>/auto-compact.json` `{ "enabled": true, "threshold": 78 }`, hot-read.
- All decisions logged to the agent EventLog (`compaction: ...`).

## Residual risk (accepted, needs owner follow-up)
With glm declaring 1M, a 78% threshold is ~817k - still above the 163k real limit of cascade peers.
Correcting the declared `contextWindow` for the ollama models in `~/.pi/agent/models.json`
(1M -> realistic) is what makes the trigger fire in time.

## Tests
- no compaction while under threshold; skips queued (streamingBehavior) prompts
- compacts + awaits at/over threshold on an idle prompt
- turn_end compaction queues exactly one resume; no resume when the turn ended with a final answer
- resume re-arms only after usage drops back under threshold
- soft error ("Nothing to compact") does not drop the prompt; hard error logs and continues
- config file parsed, clamped, hot-reloaded
close_reason: Closed

comments.text:
Independent confirmation + today's occurrence (cross-check of the 16:44 flow review). This is not theoretical: data/daemon.log (lines ~220-266) shows a DNS outage (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND api.telegram.org) where outbound sends died silently:
  [bot] deliver failed: HttpError ... sendMessage failed   (pibot-dev bot)

Suggested: event-log + a one-line owner notice on final push failure of a user turn, and/or a small on-disk outbound queue flushed by the same recovery probe that flushes dead letters.

title: Telegram push: mismatched HTML entities drop the whole message
description: Sep 18: a bot push to the owner chat (161427550) failed with 400 Bad Request: can't parse entities: Unmatched end tag at byte offset 604, expected "", found "". The message was lost — same user-visible symptom as the silent-turn bug. Cause: toTelegramHtml() in src/transports/telegram.ts runs three sequential regex passes over the escaped text (**bold**, *italic*, `code`). Sequential passes can cross tags when delimiters overlap (e.g. `a *b` c*), producing HTML Telegram refuses. push() then has no fallback: the sendMessage call throws and nothing arrives. Fix: single-pass, stack-disciplined conversion that cannot emit crossed tags, plus a plain-text degrade path so a formatting rejection never costs the message.
close_reason: Fixed in d1f4046: toTelegramHtml rewritten as a single stack-disciplined pass (no crossed tags possible) + plain-text degrade on a can't-parse-entities 400, incl. the sendRichMessage path. Reproduced the real rejection at byte 604 before the fix. 7 tests; deployed and harness-verified.

title: Decide: wire the durable satellite into the daemon, or retire the phase-1 goal
description:
`src/durable/satellite.ts` exports `openSatellite({provider, workspaceDir, storageDir, modelId, credentials})` returning `Satellite { ask, resume, harness, root }`, with `ask()` implemented as `root.submit(...).wait()` plus an exact answer-entry lookup. It has exactly one caller: scripts/durable-satellite.mts.

pibot-icv recorded a three-phase plan: (1) prototype a pi-durable harness for ONE satellite agent on the workshop box with Telegram as a surface/client; (2) keep pibot core on pi-coding-agent 1.0 meanwhile; (3) revisit a full core migration only after the satellite proves checkpoint/resume + multi-surface value. Phase 2 is done and pibot-icv.1 is closed. Phase 1 - the production satellite wiring - has not started: no daemon-owned satellite, no `attachTelegramSurface` caller outside tests and the CLI script, no `data/satellite/` directory.

So the only production pi-durable consumer remains the background task ledger (src/durable/task-ledger.ts). The "durable satellite" code is a well-tested seam that proves nothing in production because nothing runs it.

Scope to decide:

- Either wire it: daemon-owned satellite instance, its storage dir, its outbox (blocked on pibot-qy88 for the outbox/lock prerequisites) and a live round-trip verification; or
- Retire the phase-1 goal explicitly and record that core stays on pi-coding-agent 1.0, so the seam does not read as half-finished work forever.

Open sub-question from pibot-icv: the link-triage env flags were lost with the vanished `.env` (owner to restore/migrate) - the satellite entry reads `--provider`/`--model` and credentials from the shared auth.json, so confirm what the satellite still needs from the owner.

Depends on pibot-cea8 (a second writer needs the lock) and pibot-qy88 (a durable outbox to deliver into).
acceptance_criteria: Either a daemon-owned satellite with a verified live round-trip exists and is documented, or pibot-icv records the retirement of the phase-1 goal and the reason; the seam is no longer an unowned half-finished path.
notes:
DECISION: RETIRE the phase-1 daemon-owned-satellite goal. Do not wire a second harness into the daemon. Recorded in docs/durable-satellite-decision.md.

WHY (evidence gathered before deciding):

1. Capability gap is the whole product, not a seam. The satellite registers exactly ONE tool — list_workspace (read-only, 200 filenames) at src/durable/satellite.ts:26. A pibot agent on pi-coding-agent gets 28 capability definitions (src/core/capabilities.ts: link-triage, speech, avatar, dictionary, scheduler, tasks, commitments, research-intake, memory, calendar-read/write, gmail-read, linear, skills, knowledge, vault-file, docs-file, agent-comms, questions, telegram-send, …) backed by 29 plugins in src/plugins/ registering 89 tools, plus skills, long-term memory, cascade, heartbeat, proactive scheduling, and SessionManager sessions (src/core/agent-manager.ts:271). pi-durable DOES ship CodingTools (@earendil-works/pi-durable/tools → read/write/edit/bash), so the mechanical part exists — but "wire the satellite" is not 4 tools, it is reimplementing the capability registry, plugin model, agent factory, skills, memory and session store on a second harness. That is phase 3 (full core migration), and phase 3 was explicitly gated on phase 1 proving value in production, which never happened.

2. The seam-value already shipped, elsewhere. Checkpoint/resume + exactly-once-by-requestId is now delivered in production without a second harness: src/durable/task-ledger.ts (background tasks), src/durable/storage-lock.ts (pibot-cea8), src/durable/compact-ledger.ts (pibot-b708), src/core/delivery-ledger.ts (pibot-qy88), src/core/question-store.ts (pibot-jciq), src/core/scheduler.ts claim/settle (pibot-awhs). Targeted durable state on the existing stack, far smaller blast radius.

3. Two harnesses in one daemon = duplication: two storage dirs, two lock holders, two model provider stacks, two task schedulers, two credential resolutions, two crash-resume paths — for concerns the daemon now already covers.

4. The prerequisites finishing argues AGAINST wiring: pibot-cea8 (lock) exists because a second writer is dangerous; pibot-qy88 (durable outbox) exists because the daemon own delivery needed exactly the guarantee the satellite was supposed to provide. They made the daemon durable; they did not make a second harness necessary.

WHAT LANDED:
- docs/durable-satellite-decision.md — the decision, the four reasons with evidence, the table of which bead now provides which durable property, what stays, and the three questions that must be answered before reopening (capability surface, where SessionManager sessions live during/after migration, rollback plan).
- src/durable/satellite.ts + src/durable/telegram-surface.ts — header comments now say PROTOTYPE, no production caller, point at the decision doc, and telegram-surface explicitly disclaims confusion with src/core/delivery-ledger.ts (the production answer). Behaviour unchanged.
- docs/durable-ledger.md — new "Status of the durable satellite" section.
- src/durable/satellite.test.ts — new guard test "is imported only by the CLI script, never by the daemon or a plugin": walks src/ and scripts/, asserts the importer set of durable/satellite.js|durable/telegram-surface.js is exactly ["scripts/durable-satellite.mts"]. If a production module ever imports the seam, the documented decision is stale and gets made again deliberately rather than by drift. The seam stays tested and unskipped, not abandoned-by-neglect.

NOT DONE, deliberately: nothing was deleted. scripts/durable-satellite.mts stays as the prototype entry (and still refuses a live ledger dir via assertNotLiveLedger).

Gates: npx tsc --noEmit clean; npx vitest run 148 files / 2778 tests pass.

title: No cross-process lock on the pi-durable JSONL ledger directory
description:
The JSONL storage backend shipped by pi-durable has no cross-process lock. `openNodeJsonlStorage(dir)` in `node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-durable/dist/storage/jsonl/node.js` opens/creates `main.jsonl` plus `doc-<id>.jsonl` / `task-<id>.jsonl` sidecars with no `O_EXCL`, no lockfile and no PID record. Two processes pointed at the same directory will both append commit markers and interleave sidecars.

Today the only guard is the daemon PID lock at src/index.ts:68-81:

```
const lockFile = path.join(config.dataDir, "pibot.lock");
if (fs.existsSync(lockFile)) { ...stale check... }
fs.writeFileSync(lockFile, String(process.pid));
```

That protects `data/durable/tasks` (created at src/index.ts:266) only as long as every writer is the daemon.

The exposure:

- scripts/durable-satellite.mts takes `--storage-dir` on the command line. Pointed at `data/durable/tasks` it corrupts the live ledger, and nothing stops that.
- The planned production satellite (pibot-icv phase 3: "daemon-owned satellite") means a second writer by design.
- A stale-lock takeover (`/* stale lock */` branch) is not atomic: two processes can both decide the lock is stale and both write. It also only guards against same-dataDir invocations.

Scope to fix:

- Add a lock guard for the ledger directory: an owner-only lockfile created with `O_EXCL` (or `flock`) inside `openTaskLedger()` when `storageDir` is used, released on `close()`, with a clear error naming the holder.
- Document that `scripts/durable-satellite.mts --storage-dir` must never point at a live ledger, and make the satellite entry refuse a directory that already holds `main.jsonl` unless explicitly overridden.
- Treat a JSONL corruption error (`JsonlCorruptionError`) as a hard stop with an owner-visible message, never a silent reopen.

Related: pibot-icv (the satellite path that creates the second writer), pibot-qy88 and pibot-jciq (other in-memory durability gaps on the same code).
acceptance_criteria: A second openTaskLedger on a live storageDir fails fast with the holder named; close() releases the lock; a corrupt ledger stops the daemon with an owner-visible message rather than reopening silently; a test opens the same dir twice.
notes:
Implemented and closed.

WHAT WAS WRONG
openNodeJsonlStorage(dir) opens main.jsonl and its doc-/task- sidecars with no O_EXCL,
no lockfile and no PID record. The only guard was the daemon PID lock in src/index.ts,
which covers data/durable/tasks only while every writer happens to be that one daemon.
scripts/durable-satellite.mts --storage-dir data/durable/tasks walked straight past it,
and the stale-lock takeover in index.ts was not atomic (two processes could both decide
the lock was stale and both write).

WHAT LANDED
- src/durable/storage-lock.ts (NEW)
  - `lockStorageDir(dir, {label?, onStaleTakeover?})` — creates `<dir>/.pibot-ledger.lock`
    with flag "wx" (O_EXCL) and mode 0600, payload {pid, host, command, acquiredAt}.
    Returns `{dir, path, release()}`. `release()` only unlinks a record that is still
    ours, so a takeover by another process is never undone from here; it is idempotent.
  - `StorageLockedError` carries `.holder` and `.dir`; the message names pid, host,
    command and acquisition time, and says what to do (use another directory or stop
    the holder).
  - Stale takeover: a lock whose pid is provably dead ON THIS HOST is unlinked and the
    O_EXCL create is retried, so exactly one of two racers wins the create and the loser
    reports the winner. A lock recorded on ANOTHER HOST is never stolen — its liveness
    cannot be probed from here. `EPERM` from `process.kill(pid, 0)` counts as alive.
    An unreadable lock record is treated as stale rather than blocking forever.
  - `assertNotLiveLedger(dir, {force})` — refuses a directory that already contains
    main.jsonl unless forced.
- src/durable/task-ledger.ts
  - `openTaskLedger({runner, storageDir, now?, label?})` takes the lock before opening
    storage and releases it if opening fails.
  - `close()` releases the lock in a `finally`.
  - NEW `LedgerUnreadableError` — any failure opening storage or the harness is wrapped
    with an owner-visible message naming the directory and telling the reader not to
    delete it silently. This is the "hard stop, never a silent reopen" requirement.
- src/durable/satellite.ts — `openSatellite` takes the same lock, releases it on a failed
  open, and gained a public `close()` (the `Satellite` interface now declares it) that
  closes the harness and frees the directory.
- scripts/durable-satellite.mts — calls `assertNotLiveLedger(storageDir, {force:
  --force-live})` and exits 4 with the reason; awaits `satellite.close()` in a `finally`.
  The header comment now documents why --storage-dir must never point at a live ledger.
- src/index.ts — passes `label: "daemon"`; a failed open is captured into
  `ledgerUnavailable` instead of only being logged, and after `bot.start()` the owner
  gets a real message: "⚠️ Durable tasks are OFF for this run. The task ledger at <dir>
  could not be opened: <reason>". Previously the daemon ran with `agents.tasks =
  undefined` and the owner was never told durable tasks had silently disappeared.

TESTS
- src/durable/storage-lock.test.ts (NEW, 11 tests): owner-only lock creation and payload;
  a second open of a live-owned directory fails naming the holder; stale takeover of a
  dead pid; a foreign-host lock is never stolen; an unparsable lock is stale; release is
  idempotent and never deletes someone else's record; assertNotLiveLedger allows an empty
  dir and refuses one holding main.jsonl; openTaskLedger holds the dir, rejects the second
  writer, frees it on close, reopens with contents intact; a corrupt main.jsonl stops with
  LedgerUnreadableError/JsonlCorruptionError and leaves no lock behind; an in-memory
  ledger takes no lock.
- src/durable/satellite.test.ts — the crash/resume and resume-on-open tests used to open
  one storageDir twice, which the lock now correctly forbids. They close the first
  satellite before reopening (and drop the copied lock in the crash-simulation case).

GATES: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `npx vitest run` 147 files / 2771 tests pass.

NOT CHANGED (deliberate)
- The daemon PID lock in src/index.ts is untouched. It guards getUpdates polling, which is
  a different resource; the new lock guards the ledger directory and works for any writer.
- The JSONL backend itself is not patched (node_modules). Both first-party entry points
  (task ledger, satellite) now take the advisory lock; anything that bypasses them is
  outside what this repo can enforce, which is why the satellite entry also refuses a
  populated directory rather than relying on the lock alone.
close_reason: O_EXCL storage-dir lock with named holder, stale takeover, corruption hard-stop, satellite refuses live ledger

title: Scheduler fire is not durable: a crash inside the 250ms save debounce loses a one-shot
description:
src/core/scheduler.ts:87-95 batches persistence:

```
private save(): void {
  if (this.saveTimer) return;
  this.saveTimer = setTimeout(() => { this.saveTimer = null; this.flush(); }, 250);
}
```

`flush()` writes the whole job set to `data/schedules.json` with `writeJsonAtomic`. So there is a window of up to 250 ms — longer under load — in which a job has been marked fired/done in memory but the file still says `pending`.

Failure: a one-shot fires (side effect delivered: a Telegram reminder is sent), the process dies before `flush()`. On reopen `load()` sees `status: "pending"` and the job fires again. The reverse also holds: a `repeat` job whose occurrence was consumed but whose next `dueAt` was not yet computed can double-fire.

Second, separate behaviour that deserves to be explicit rather than changed blindly: src/core/scheduler.ts:73 prunes any pending non-repeating job whose `dueAt + 86400e3 < now` by marking it `done`, with the comment "missed while offline > 1 day; don't spam old fires". A missed reminder older than a day therefore disappears with no owner-visible record and no catch-up. That may be the right policy, but it is currently indistinguishable from a job that actually fired.

Scope to fix:

- Make the fire transition durable before the side effect is dispatched (or at minimum flush synchronously on fire), so a restart cannot re-fire an already-delivered reminder.
- Distinguish "fired" from "pruned as missed" in the persisted state and in whatever the owner sees.
- Keep `snooze` persistence consistent with the same rule.
- Do not silently change the 1-day prune policy without saying so; record it as a decision.

Related: pibot-glm (drain-then-terminate restart path) narrows this window but does not close it.
acceptance_criteria: A job that fired and was delivered is never re-fired after an unclean kill; a job pruned as missed while offline is recorded as missed, not as fired; flush cost stays reasonable for a 20-item-per-agent set (measure it).
notes:
Implemented and closed.

WHAT WAS WRONG
1. `fireOnce` dispatched the side effect, then mutated state, then called the
   debounced `save()` (250 ms). A kill inside that window left schedules.json
   saying `pending`, so the reopened daemon re-fired an already-delivered reminder.
2. The boot prune marked stale one-shots `done` with no record of why, making a
   reminder that never went out look identical to one that fired.

THE FIX — claim the outcome on disk BEFORE dispatch
`Scheduler.claimOccurrence()` writes the POST-fire state to disk before the side
effect leaves the process:

    firing: { claimedAt, dueAtAtFire, firedCount: n+1, nextDueAt? }

`nextDueAt` is computed at claim time, so the claim fully determines the outcome and
boot has nothing left to decide. On a clean settle `settleOccurrence()` drops the
claim and `saveNow()` commits. At boot, a `pending` job still carrying `firing` is
finished exactly as if delivery had happened (repeat → its claimed next slot, one-shot
→ `done`/`fired`) and the loss is reported on the console.

THE TRADE, STATED EXPLICITLY
A crash between claim and delivery loses one occurrence — the job reads as fired.
A crash after delivery can no longer repeat it. That is the direction the issue asks
for: a missed reminder is recoverable, an uninvited duplicate is not. Anyone reading
this later should not "fix" it back into at-least-once.

`saveNow()` (immediate flush) replaces the debounced `save()` for every transition
inside `fireOnce` and for the boot prune. Measured cost on a 20-job set: well under
1 ms per flush (asserted < 15 ms in the test), so synchronous persistence is not a
throughput concern at this scale. Ordinary CRUD (create/cancel/snooze) keeps the
debounce — a lost frame there is harmless and rebuilt from intent.

"MISSED" IS NOW A RECORDED OUTCOME, NOT AN IMPLICIT ONE
- `Schedule.outcome?: "fired" | "missed"` and `Schedule.missedAt?` (src/core/types.ts).
- The boot prune sets `outcome = "missed"`, `missedAt = now`, logs a summary, and
  flushes immediately so a second boot cannot re-decide it. The 1-day catch-up
  window is UNCHANGED (exported as `MISSED_AFTER_MS` so the policy is named, not
  buried in a literal) — this issue asked for the record, not a policy change.
- `Scheduler.recentMissed(agentId?, withinMs = 7 days)` exposes them, and `/status`
  now appends `missed while offline: N — "title" (when), …` so the owner sees that a
  reminder was skipped instead of assuming it went out.
- Snooze state stays on the same rule: a fire that defers to a snooze window, or a
  heartbeat that skips a beat, uses the debounced save (no side effect was dispatched
  yet); a fire that closes the job uses `saveNow()`.

FILES
- src/core/scheduler.ts — `claimOccurrence`, `settleOccurrence`, `finish(job, outcome)`,
  `saveNow`, `MISSED_AFTER_MS`, `recentMissed`, boot resolution of `firing`, interrupted-
  job reporting, `finish()` on the internal repeat-exhausted path.
- src/core/types.ts — `Schedule.outcome`, `missedAt`, `firing`.
- src/core/commands.ts — `/status` reports missed schedules.
- src/core/scheduler.test.ts — 7 new tests: claim visible on disk from inside the
  delivery callback; mid-fire one-shot NOT re-fired after restart and settled as
  fired; repeat job settled to its claimed next slot; mid-fire boot report; repeat
  next-occurrence durability across a clean stop; snooze-during-fire persistence;
  measured flush cost. The old "drops stale one-shots" test now asserts the missed
  outcome instead of a vanished job.

GATES: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `npx vitest run` 146 files / 2760 tests pass.

RELATED: pibot-glm (drain-then-terminate restart) narrows the window further but is
independent; this fix closes the re-fire regardless of how the process dies.
close_reason: Fire claims its post-fire state on disk before dispatch; missed is a recorded outcome

title: Jev shadow evaluation for skill evolution
description:
## Goal
Evaluate Jev as a typed, advisory judge in PiBot's existing skill self-evolution loop while the current 1-5 judge and deterministic promotion policy remain authoritative.

## Scope
- Build consented, independent replay cases from eligible staged or historical skills, with verified baseline and candidate versions and blinded human labels.
- Add a default-off, per-agent, provider/data-scoped shadow observer at the probe/judge boundary. Bound input, calls, queue, timeout, and metadata retention; keep private text out of logs.
- Compare Jev and current-judge outcomes with human labels, including disagreements, severe misses, false reviews, unavailable results, latency, and cost.
- Return a decision report for owner review before any active gate or promotion-policy change.

## Non-goals
No replacement of the current judge, no Jev promotion/veto, no live deployment, and no link-triage changes under this epic.

## Success Criteria
Shadow outcomes cannot change scores, staging, promotion, announcements, or backlog closure; boundary tests cover success and all fallback classes. Replay provenance and data permission are documented. The report states evidence and limitations. Any active gate requires a separate approved decision.

## Spec

title: No wall-clock cap on a user turn — a hung model leaves the owner in silence

Evidence (already happened): data/daemon.log.old:1549 region — '[telegram] <- /cancel' twice, then 'suppressed duplicate send to chat 161427550'; the second /cancel got no reply. title: pi-durable task ledger log grows without bound — no compaction of main.jsonl
description:
`data/durable/tasks/main.jsonl` is 717 lines / 334 KB and `data/durable/tasks/doc-6.jsonl` is 363 lines / 343 KB (measured 2026-10-28). Both only grow.

Two things were conflated when this was first assumed to be self-limiting:

1. `KEEP_FINISHED = 200` in src/durable/task-ledger.ts prunes finished task entries *inside* the ledger document (`prune(doc)` in the notify phase). That bounds the document's logical size, not the on-disk log.
2. The JSONL backend does reclaim sidecars — `reclaimSidecars()` in node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-durable/dist/storage/jsonl/storage.js:382 — but the commit markers in `main.jsonl` are never compacted. Every historical revision of the ledger doc stays on disk with its full sidecar replay.

At the current rate the ledger is a few MB and harmless. The reason to care now is that startup replays the log: boot time and memory for `openTaskLedger()` grow with it, and a task-heavy period (dozens of long transcription runs) multiplies it.

Scope:

- Measure current replay cost at boot (time from `openTaskLedger` start to ready) and project it against a 10x log.
- Find the supported compaction/reclaim entry point in the backend (there is `reclaimSidecars`, and documents can be retired/re-based); if none is public, record that as an upstream gap and add a supervised offline rewrite instead of hand-editing the file.
- Any rewrite must be done with the ledger closed and the lock held (see pibot-cea8) and must preserve unfinished tasks and their `requests` idempotency map.

Related: pibot-cea8 (lock), pibot-icv (audit context).
acceptance_criteria: Boot replay cost is measured and documented; either a supported compaction path is used or an upstream gap is recorded with a safe offline rewrite procedure; a rewrite preserves unfinished tasks and the requests idempotency map.

title: heartbeat digest panel: pending count is structurally ≥1 (ticks log themselves into the pending window) — misleading "N events pending, last run Xh" line
description: Worker (Oct 7) reported consolidation "stalled: 5 events pending, last run 21h across 6+ consecutive ticks". Evidence says the runner is healthy (last run Oct 6 19:57 consumed 6 events cleanly; zero distill failures in daemon.log) and the panel line was arithmetically correct — but misleading by construction: every heartbeat tick appends its maintenance+heartbeat pair to state/events.jsonl AFTER the consolidation cursor, so post-run ticks always re-create pending events (including the stall report itself — self-consuming pending window). Combined with worker confabulating 6+ maintain:consolidate logs that never appear in events.jsonl/maintenance.jsonl, the panel line drove a false incident. Fix sketch: exclude the agent s own tick-generated (maintenance/heartbeat) entries from the pending count and/or show "N pending (ticks: k)" with last-tick age; optionally auto-run consolidation when pending consists only of self-referential tick entries (deterministic summary, no model call).

title: Encrypt the dashboard session stores (web-auth-secret, web-sessions.json)
description:
Two credential files remain plaintext outside the sops stores, both in data/ (0600, gitignored):
- web-auth-secret — 32 bytes of HMAC key that signs session cookies. Boot-decryptable once, so it can live in settings.enc.json or its own .enc.json.
- web-sessions.json — live session tokens (12h TTL), i.e. usable dashboard credentials. Written on login/logout, so encrypting means a sops call per auth event (rare, acceptable).

Either encrypt both, or stop persisting sessions at all (in-memory only, re-auth after a restart) — that may be the better design: sessions arguably need not survive a restart, and then web-auth-secret is the only thing to protect.

title: ops: drain-then-self-terminate restart path (no delayed fuses)
description: Restarting the daemon kills pibot-dev's in-flight turn (agent runs inside the daemon), so restarts need a delayed fuse — which the launchd-run verifier proved fragile (reaped background children; launchd's minimal PATH had no npx/sops for the verify chain). Proper flow: a 'pibot restart' that replies → drains the per-chat outbox → self-terminates → launchd respawns instantly; post-boot notifyBoot (5283e3a) then confirms automatically. Note: launchd-run scripts need absolute tool paths.

title: Dead-letter cap silently breaks the 'your message is saved' promise
description:
cascade.queueDead() truncates to the last 100 entries ('the oldest unsent messages are the least relevant') with no log, event, or owner notice — while the user was explicitly told 'Your message is saved — top up at the provider console and it will be processed automatically once credits return' (core/bot.ts unavailableNotice). During a long multi-provider outage the oldest queued owner messages are therefore discarded after a promise that they were kept. Noted only as a parenthetical in the pibot-dev review's L8.

Fix sketch: when truncating, events.log a 'system' entry naming how many queued messages were dropped, and push one owner notice ('N older queued messages were dropped after the queue hit its 100-message cap'). Consider raising the cap or spilling to a file rather than dropping user text.

title: Reply media attachments fail silently (no event, no notice)
description:
core/bot.ts onSessionEvent: MEDIA lines from splitMediaLines are sent with void t.sendMedia(...).then(ok => events.log(media), e => console.error('[bot] media send failed:', e)). A failed attachment therefore leaves the text reply without its file and leaves only a console line — no event-log entry, no owner-visible signal — while the sibling case (transport has no sendMedia) is explicitly event-logged ('media dropped: ...') after the Sep 16 creator incident.

Fix sketch: mirror the existing 'media dropped' handling on the failure path: events.log(agentId, 'system', 'media send failed: <source> — <error>') and append one short notice to the already-sent text (or a follow-up line) so the owner knows a file was missing.
close_reason: Fixed in 9e0bb3b: a failed reply attachment now logs an event ('media send failed: <file> — <error>') and tells the owner which file did not arrive, instead of only console.error. 2 bot tests. Deployed, harness 4/4.

title: docs/reliability-audit-2026-10-24.md documents a stale LedgerStatus (no partial/blocked)
description:
docs/reliability-audit-2026-10-24.md:6 describes the task ledger with an earlier `LedgerStatus` shape. The live type in src/durable/task-ledger.ts is:

```
export type LedgerStatus = "queued" | "running" | "done" | "partial" | "blocked" | "failed" | "cancelled";
```

`partial` and `blocked` were added with the verified-completion gate (bd pibot-zy70) and the destination-aware delivery checks (bd pibot-cida): a task that ran but whose delivered medium/destination/account/id-namespace did not match the declared expectation is `partial`, and a `BlockedError` is `blocked`. The audit doc predates both, so a reader comparing the doc to the code sees a mismatch and cannot tell which is authoritative.

Fix: update the doc section to the current shape and mention the delivery gate, or add a dated correction note pointing at src/durable/task-ledger.ts. Keep the original audit text as history rather than silently rewriting a dated audit.
